audits.title: 708 An Audit of Blood Transfusion Prescription in Peri-Operative Orthopaedic Patients for Those with and Without a Coronary History
audits.standard: NICE Blood Transfusion Guidance (2015): threshold Hb <70 g/L, target 70–90 g/L; altered threshold only for acute coronary syndrome
audits.setting: Secondary care orthopaedic department, Liverpool University Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 21.4% transfused in line with NICE threshold and targets; average Hb threshold 75.5 (range 60–110); 54.2% prescribed 1 unit at a time.

audits.other_findings: Most common reason for altered threshold was an inconsistently defined 'coronary history', yet 0% had an ACS; iron deficiency anaemia identified in 11.4% and treated pre-operatively in 7%.
audits.citation: Wauchope E, Letch E. 708 An Audit of Blood Transfusion Prescription in Peri-Operative Orthopaedic Patients for Those with and Without a Coronary History. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.029.

audits.title: 513 A Clinical Audit on the Use of Red Cell Transfusions in a DGH’s Trauma and Orthopaedics Ward
audits.standard: Local Trust blood transfusion guideline (haemoglobin thresholds)
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics ward, district general hospital (Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 34 units across 16 patients; 73.5% of transfusions inappropriate (patient did not meet the guideline Hb threshold); 26.4% for active haemorrhage; TACO assessment completed in 58.8%.

audits.intervention: Teaching session for all rotational doctors on the Trust guideline; induction booklet highlighting the guideline.

cycle2.result: 11 units transfused; inappropriate transfusions 45.5%; 18.2% for active haemorrhage; TACO assessment 90.9%.

audits.other_findings: No transfusions were for major haemorrhage.
audits.citation: Qamar A, Fung A. 513 A Clinical Audit on the Use of Red Cell Transfusions in a DGH’s Trauma and Orthopaedics Ward. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.242.

audits.title: WP4.6 - Reducing Unnecessary Transfusion of Blood Products – A Quality Improvement Project in a General Surgical Department in a District General Hospital
audits.setting: General surgical department, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 112 units in 42 patients; 45 units (40.2%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 23 units (20.5%) transfused back-to-back inappropriately.

audits.intervention: Departmental teaching sessions and posters of NICE transfusion thresholds on surgical wards.

cycle2.result: 133 units in 43 patients; 67 units (50.4%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 6 units (4.51%) back-to-back inappropriately.

audits.other_findings: Transfusion reactions fell from 2 (1.79%) to none; estimated saving £1830 over four months (£5493 per year).
audits.citation: Arbis A, Hamawandi A, Donnellan I. WP4.6 - Reducing Unnecessary Transfusion of Blood Products – A Quality Improvement Project in a General Surgical Department in a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.155.

audits.title: 535 A Clinical Audit of Out-of-Hours Red Cell Transfusions in a Regional Hospital
audits.standard: NICE blood transfusion guidelines, with five local criteria for appropriate out-of-hours transfusion

cycle1.result: 70.6% of 51 out-of-hours RCC units were appropriate; 29.4% not indicated

audits.intervention: Planned: verbal proforma before re-audit and guidelines on appropriate requests
audits.other_findings: Active haemorrhage in 31.4% and symptomatic anaemia in 51%; no transfusion complications recorded.
audits.citation: Dimond D, Ronayne C, Coyle P, Khan S, Kehoe A. 535 A Clinical Audit of Out-of-Hours Red Cell Transfusions in a Regional Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.256.

audits.title:
Transfusion in critical care – a
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    regional audit of current practice
audits.standard: UK best practice: restrictive transfusion threshold of haemoglobin below 70 g/l in stable non-bleeding patients
audits.setting: Nine intensive care units in the Wessex regional network

cycle1.result: Median pre-transfusion Hb 73 (68-77 [53-106]) g/l; only 34% of episodes used a threshold below 70 g/l.

audits.other_findings: 444 transfusions, 148 excluded; in patients without cardiac disease only 36% used the below 70 g/l threshold.
audits.citation:
Plumb J, Taylor M, Clissold E, Grocott M, Gill R, . Transfusion in critical care – a
                    <scp>UK</scp>
                    regional audit of current practice. Anaesthesia. 2017;72(5):633-640. doi:10.1111/anae.13824.
